Definition: from a compound of G2090 and the base of G4197; (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means:--ability.
BiblicalUsage: euporéō turns up where the Bible says to prosper, to be well off. In Acts 11:29, the text says "every man according to his ability."
TheologicalSignificance: Out of euporéō I do not force more than it gives: to prosper, to be well off.
RelatedEvents: Relief Sent to Judea in the Famine
